title: Character faces: faceted bodies with anime face textures
question: Is this the direction for the game's characters, and which attempt?

options.label: Before · claude-facet attempt-04
options.note: Round 1's faceted figures: box eyes, box glasses and brows on an eight-sided head. What I see: the eyes are two dark boxes behind box glasses, which is the blank stare.

options.label: cf-01 · face texture on the old head
options.note: Change: the box eyes, glasses, brows and Eric's stubble shell come off; a painted face texture (eyes, brows, nose, mouth, glasses, Eric's stubble) is projected onto the front of the same eight-sided head, lit like the rest. Thin temple bars stay as geometry. What I see: it reads as an anime face for the first time, with the portraits' half-lidded eyes and dark upper lash line. A facet edge runs down the middle of the face, so one half is lighter than the other. Mio's irises come out grey, not light tan.

options.label: cf-02 · + flat face shading
options.note: Change: every corner of the textured front gets one forward-facing normal, so the face shades as one plane and the facet edges no longer cut across the eyes. Geometry unchanged. What I see: the face is one even tone and the split is gone. The face area is now brighter than the head's sides, and that edge shows in three-quarter view.

options.label: cf-03 · + smoother face front
options.note: Change: the front 120 degrees of the head are seven narrow sides instead of three wide ones (the back keeps five flat sides), so the face sits on a gently curved front. What I see: the cheeks turn a little more smoothly in three-quarter view. From the front it looks almost the same as cf-02.

options.label: cf-04 · + ink outline
options.note: Change: a dark outline round every part (the inverted hull from claude-ink attempt-07, 8 mm wide here, 5 mm on small parts). This is level 1 of both series below. What I see: the outline separates head, hair and body. The face itself is unchanged. At the game camera the face is about 8 pixels across, seen from above, and the eyes don't read; you see skin, glasses glint and hair.

options.label: cf-05 · simplification level 2
options.note: From cf-04, one change: simpler shapes. Two fewer sides on the body shapes, four-sided limbs, six-sided hair, no shoe soles. What I see: blockier shapes. At the game camera it looks almost the same as cf-04.

options.label: cf-06 · simplification level 3
options.note: From cf-05, one change: simplest. Five-sided body shapes and hair, and no hands, soles, cuffs, side strand or extra hair pieces. What I see: the plainest version, with no hands and simpler hair. The glasses' side bars stick out past Mio's hair, and at the game camera it looks about the same as cf-05.

options.label: cf-07 · stylization level 2
options.note: From cf-04, one change: proportions pushed toward chibi. Head 1.3 times bigger, legs 0.85 as long. What I see: a bigger head and shorter legs. In the game the head is easier to pick out, but the face still doesn't read.

options.label: cf-08 · stylization level 3
options.note: From cf-07, one change: further toward chibi. Head 1.65 times bigger, legs 0.7 as long. What I see: at the game camera this is the first level where the face shows as a face (eyes and glasses as dark marks), mostly on desktop. Up close Eric's head looks large and blocky.

options.label: cf-09 · + bolder face marks
options.note: From cf-04, one change: the face texture's dark lines (lashes, pupils, brows, frames, mouth, Eric's stubble) spread by 3 pixels with a round brush, for the game camera. What I see: in the game the face is a little darker but not clearer than cf-04. Up close the bolder lines make Mio look like she's scowling, and Eric's stubble turns into dashes.

options.label: cf-10 · stylization 3 with the bolder face
options.note: cf-08's proportions with cf-09's face: the two changes that most help the face at the game camera, together. What I see: in the game the face reads best of the round, but the difference from cf-08 is small. Up close it has the same harsh, scowling look as cf-09.

options.label: gen-front · texture source faces
options.note: Front-facing faces from the local anime model (RDBT Anima, Euler A, 30 steps, CFG 5, 1024 square), the source of the face textures. Try 1 (seeds 101-104, plain prompt): skin came out tanned, hair strands crossed the face, and Eric went photographic on three seeds of four. Try 2 (seeds 111-114): the anime style anchors, "pale skin" and "forehead and whole face clear of hair" added; picked mio 113 and eric 112. Prompts and negatives per image: art/parts/style-concepts/claude-facetface/gen/front2/prompts.json.

options.label: gen-expr · expressions
options.note: The expressions: eyes, brows and mouth of the picked faces repainted (masked img2img with DifferentialDiffusion, denoise 0.6 and 0.72, seeds 401 and 402), the rest kept. Mio "small soft smile", Eric "surprised, eyes wide open, eyebrows raised, mouth slightly open". Picked mio 401-d60 and eric 401-d72.

options.label: gen-ref · faceted-style references
options.note: Full-body anime references asked for in a faceted low-poly look ("low poly 3d game character, faceted flat-shaded polygons, simple shapes, anime face painted on the head"), seeds 201-203. Off-model: Mio has bare legs, Eric loses his ponytail on one seed. Shown for what the model thinks the style looks like.

options.label: gen-i2i · img2img over our renders
options.note: img2img over our own renders (denoise 0.45 and 0.6, seed 301), to see how the faces could look: first over cf-04, then over the before (claude-facet attempt-04). At 0.6 the model draws anime eyes into the faceted head and keeps the body; at 0.45 it mostly keeps our faces.

links.label: Turn them, play idle and walk, swap the expressions (live 3D)

decision: Texture-face attempts rejected ('all the options like this look the same but they look like shit'); gen-front rejected. Target: gen-i2i mio-front-d60, 'if you were able to do this it would be mindboggling ... I doubt it. Prove me wrong.'
